title: Recover the axioms of a “jolie” A-linear category
as_he_states: The biconditional with a filtered union of strict monogenic projective-module subcategories is written with an inverse-direction question mark.
plausible_today: If an additive idempotent-complete category is generated, on finite sets of objects, by their finite direct sums, each such additive envelope is modeled by finite projectives over an endomorphism ring; the exact manuscript category may require fewer objects.
state_of_art: Morita projective-envelope theory is established (Abrams–Ruiz–Tomforde §1); it cannot identify the missing “jolie” axioms.
why_open: The supplied fragment omits the definition and marks the converse with a question; no documentary explanation for later abandonment was found.
worth: Worth a short archival reconstruction only after adjoining the neighboring definitional leaves; not a new Morita theorem.

title: Localizability of an action category over Spec R
as_he_states: The Spec A argument explicitly does not prove that Mod(R,C), for commutative R, is localizable over R.
plausible_today: Specify the fibrewise stack of R-actions over R-opens and prove effective descent under a chosen base-change construction. Flatness alone repairs Hom, not lifting of all actions.
state_of_art: Ferrand §1–2 verifies descent through torsors/bitorsors; CL-SA07-707 gives an exact nonflat obstruction and CL-SA07-708 the restricted repair.

worth: Worth one focused run because a precise definition and counterexamples can delimit the strongest valid statement.

title: Canonical transport between Picard automorphism categories
as_he_states: A self-flagged “À vérifier!!” asks whether the two automorphism Picard categories of a bitorsor are canonically equivalent.
plausible_today: Transport is canonical up to coherent isomorphism; after passage to a Picard band, commutativity kills inner conjugation. A strict unchosen functor is not implied.
state_of_art: Ferrand Lemma1.1 and Proposition1.2 establish the bitorsor/band formulation; K15-02 then checks generator transport under commuting-ideal condition C.
why_open: The doubt is local to coherence and choice; the later supplied pages partly answer it, so it is not an untouched open problem.
worth: Worth a short explanatory lemma in the folder commentary, with coherence conventions made explicit.

title: Homogeneous or exterior-form formulation of Frobenius
as_he_states: A marginal note suggests a homogeneous/exterior-form version of the inhomogeneous PDE calculation.
plausible_today: For a constant-rank C^r distribution (r≥1, analytic if desired) on an appropriate Banach manifold, the involutivity/integrability condition yields local integral manifolds under the standard complemented-subspace hypotheses; finite-dimensional analytic Pfaff systems are the immediate case.
state_of_art: Penot1970 Theorem1.1 gives the local analytic/Banach PDE theorem and subsequent sections the distribution formulation.
why_open: The supplied text suggests an extension of exposition; it is not evidence of a still-open Frobenius theorem.
worth: Worth a short translation of the coordinate calculation, with rank and complement hypotheses stated.

title: Dependence from an identically zero Jacobian
as_he_states: “Il faudrait faire ici … le théorème de dépendance” for holomorphic functions with identically zero Jacobian.

state_of_art: The local theorem follows by the analytic inverse/implicit theorem (Lebl1.3.8); the fragment does not identify a global dependence category.

worth: Worth a precise local formulation in the analysis appendix, not an attribution of a modern global conjecture.
